text:
alex.k: Heads-up — while exercising the Go SDK generator sample app during onboarding I hit a cancel + goroutine leak when token refresh happens mid-stream. Repro pretty small:

alex.k: Steps to repro:
1) Start generator streaming -> client fetches token, handshake completes.
2) After a few tokens, trigger auth refresh (rotate API key) so auth layer blocks waiting for new creds.
3) Cancel the request context from the app side.

alex.k: Expected: streaming generator returns quickly with ctx.Err() and all goroutines cleaned up. Observed: generator didn't return, goroutine count grows, KV cache goroutine stuck in auth refresh path.

maria.devex: can you paste the minimal sampleapp snippet you used?

alex.k: sure — simplified call site:

```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 10*time.Second)
defer cancel()

respCh := make(chan string)
go func() {
    gen, _ := client.Generator(ctx, cfg)
    for tok := range gen.Stream() {
        respCh <- tok
    }
    close(respCh)
}()

// simulate auth rotation after 1s
time.AfterFunc(1*time.Second, rotateKey)
// cancel after 3s
time.AfterFunc(3*time.Second, cancel)

for s := range respCh {
    fmt.Println(s)
}
```

alex.k: the generator's Stream() never closed in this trace; pprof showed goroutines stuck in `auth/refresh.go:42` waiting on a mutex.

jordan.sdk: hmm — this sounds like two separate concerns: (A) auth refresh path can block indefinitely if it waits on network or lock, (B) generator should select on ctx.Done in all hot loops including during handshake and while waiting for auth tokens. If the SDK's auth refresh uses a single global lock and the refresh blocks, cancel shouldn't be able to unblock consumers.

jordan.sdk: quick patch idea: make auth refresh cooperative and cancellable. e.g. in refresh loop:

```go
select {
case <-ctx.Done():
    return ctx.Err()
case <-refreshDone:
    // continue
}
```

jordan.sdk: and ensure generator's main read loop does `select { case <-ctx.Done(): return; case msg := <-recv: ... }` — everywhere we wait on network we should also wait on ctx.

alex.k: I instrumented the client, here's the log snippet (trimmed):

```
[00:00:01] handshake: started
[00:00:01] auth: refresh triggered
[00:00:02] auth: stuck waiting for server (retry loop)
[00:00:03] ctx: cancelled by app
[00:00:03] generator: still blocking on recv
```

sam.sre: can you run `GODEBUG=gctrace=1` and `go test -run TestLeak -bench . -benchmem` to capture allocs? also what Go version? we've seen subtle scheduler interactions pre-1.20.

alex.k: Go 1.21.2. I'll run bench and post results. Quick heap/alloc snapshot:

```
pprof: goroutine 112 @ auth/refresh.go:42
pprof: 19 goroutines in net/http blocked on client.Transport
```

maria.devex: thanks — sounds high priority for onboarding UX. New users hitting this during quickstart is very bad. Can we treat as P1 for next sprint? linking owners.

jordan.sdk: I'll open a defending PR that wires ctx into the auth refresh path and patches the generator loop to always select on ctx.Done. Also add unit test that simulates blocked auth + context cancel.

alex.k: that would help. For the sampleapp, maybe add a note to the README with a recommended pattern (use context.WithTimeout and ensure generator.Stream is consumed in a goroutine with defers). New users confuse this often.

maria.devex: agree. Also add a short snippet under "Troubleshooting: stuck streaming" in onboarding docs.

ci-bot: Issue created: https://redwood.company/issue/1452 "go sdk: generator doesn't close on context cancel during auth refresh" (assigned -> jordan.sdk)

sam.sre: once PR is up, can you include a small stress test (n=100 concurrent short streams with forced refresh) so we don't regress.

alex.k: will verify afterwards and post results here. thanks all :thumbsup!
